walkthroughs.body_html:
Hypothesis Testing — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Hypothesis Testing brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Hypothesis Testing.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Type I & Type II errors”?
options: Set of observed values for which H₀ is rejected. Found from significance level and distribution under H₀.
α (often 5%, 1%). Probability of rejecting H₀ when it is true (Type I error).
Type I: reject true H₀ (rate = α). Type II: fail to reject false H₀ (rate β). Power = 1 − β.
One-tailed: alternative specifies direction (e.g., p > 0.5). Two-tailed: any difference (p ≠ 0.5). Affects critical region.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “P-value”?
options: Type I: reject true H₀ (rate = α). Type II: fail to reject false H₀ (rate β). Power = 1 − β.
H₀ is the default (e.g., p = 0.5). H₁ is what we test against (one-tailed or two-tailed). Decide based on evidence.
Probability, under H₀, of observing data as extreme or more extreme than the observed. Reject H₀ if p < α.
Set of observed values for which H₀ is rejected. Found from significance level and distribution under H₀.
